column1: *** Félix de Llerena, b. about 1725, Córdoba, ANDALUSIA ***
column2: *** "Carvalho Calcagno Web Site" and "Familia Martinez Camino" *** - two other MyHeritage trees.
column3: *** THE AGREEMENT IS WORTHLESS AS CORROBORATION. *** This archive noted that the tree agreed with its own reading of "Córdova la llana" as the Spanish city, "from a direction that owes the archive nothing". *** It owes the archive nothing because it is two strangers' trees, and it may well have copied the same reasoning from the same place. *** Row 121 is answered and the answer is: no support.

column1: *** Fidel Llerena, d. 30 January 1822, son of Sancho Francisco Llerena Aguilar and María Josefa Teresa Fernandez ***
column3: The archive already knew the 1822 was tree-only, from Geneanet. *** This is the same claim arriving from a second tree, not a second source. *** The fuller names - Sancho FRANCISCO, María JOSEFA TERESA - are unsourced and must not be written into the register.

column1: *** The Brayley ascent, eleven generations to Matthew Reed of 1643 ***
column2: *** Matthew Reed: "Lightning Web Site". John Brailey: "Moore-Christian Web Site". HELEN WALKER: NOTHING AT ALL. ***
column3: *** The deep end of the ascent is unsourced. *** This archive published it flagged as "tree, not record" - which was right - but it did not say HOW thin. *** It is this thin: the oldest man on it is somebody's web site. *** The parishes and dates are still what make it testable, and testing it is now the only thing that would make it real.

column1: *** Georgina Temple, b. 23 August 1814, Haddington ***
column2: *** "1851 England & Wales Census" *** - a real record.
column3: *** One of the six. *** It puts her in a household in 1851 and is worth having.

column1: *** Mary Ann Hellen Brayley, d. 21 April 1900 ***
column2: *** "England & Wales, Death Index, 1866-1920" *** - a real record.
column3: *** One of the six. *** The death is indexed; the birth of 20 May 1843 at St Bartholomew's is not.

column1: *** Pablo Armando / Robert Paul Lerena, b. 22 February 1882, Rosario ***
column3: *** This archive does not need the tree for this *** - it has his own passport and his own enrolment card. *** But it is worth knowing that the tree's version of the central fact is itself unsourced ***, which is how the Llorens parents were able to sit beside it for years without anything objecting.

column1: *** Pierre Frederick Lerena and his two sons, dead 12 November 1999 ***
column3: *** Three deaths on one day, and not one of them is sourced. *** This archive recorded it plainly and said it should be checked against a death registration before being stated as fact. *** That warning now has a number behind it and should be treated as binding. ***

column1: # *** WHAT THIS DOES NOT MEAN. ***
# It does not mean the tree is wrong. An unsourced entry can be perfectly correct - it may rest on a
# document in somebody's drawer, or on a memory, or on a record whose citation was never typed in.
# *** It means the tree cannot be used as EVIDENCE, only as a set of LEADS *** - and that a lead with
# a parish and a date on it is worth a great deal more than one without, because it can be tested.
# *** WHAT IT MEANS FOR THE ARCHIVE. ***
# The register stays at 278. *** Nothing from the tree is promoted on the tree's say-so. *** What the
# import has actually bought is a WORK LIST: four Uruguayan departments, a Devon parish with three
# deaths in three days, three street addresses, and a date in November 1999 to check.
